newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 12.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The regional government office for Ostrava-Mariansky Hory in Tachov has come up with a controversial plan to contribute to the price of the air tickets if the local Roma (gypsy) families are willing to emmigrate to Canada. Many groups have called the plan racist.

- The floods which effected Moravia and Silesia last month caused approximately 60 billion crowns worth of damages, according to the Ministry of the Environment. Environment Minister, Jiri Skalicky, stated that this is the first serious figure the Ministry has been able to release.
- The local economy, in spite of the pessimistic forecasts in the beginning of this year, actually appears to be showing some growth.

- The Czech Statistic Office has shown a decrease of 1.2 percent in the efficiency of the Construction industry, showing that construction has still not recovered from the blow it received early in the year from the heavy frosts.

- Value Bill, a company made up of Patria Finance (40 percent), Pernod Ricard (40 percent) and Karel Scharzenberg, has presented the Finance Ministry with a proposal for the privatisation of 89 percent of Jan Becher - Karlovarska Becherovka, according to Vladimir Kreidl from Patria Finance.

- The Czech Republic, Egypt and Portugal are the three countries in which Intel is considering building their new plant for the manufacture and testing of microprocessers. The plant, which should cost $500 million to build, should eventually employ 6,000 employees, according to Vaclav Petricek from the Ministry of Trade and Industry.

- Shares of companies effected by the recent flooding in Moravia and Silesia have not shown a significant decrease in value, according to financial experts. The only visable effect that can be seen is a slight increase in the value of construction company shares and a decrease in the value of shares of Ceska Pojistovna and Komercni Banka.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Czech industrial manufacturers showed a record growth of 7.9 percent in production in June as compared to June a year ago. While this result was influenced by an extra working day, even after taking this factor into account the increase would be 5.3 percent, the largest increase this year.
- The Czech Chamber of Commerce has appealed to the government to not penalise companies effected by last month's floods which are late with insurance payments and taxes.
- Ceske Drahy is refusing to recompense firms for secondary damages suffered during the February rail strikes, according to a spokesman for Ceske Drahy, Petr Hoffman.

- Zetor Brno, a.s., the only domestic manufacturer of tractors, has signed a contract with Brazil's Agrale for the manufacture of tractors in Brazil using Zetor components, according to the management of Zetor.

PRAVO - Ostrava's Nova Hut, in spite of the recent flooding in its area, posted a gross profit of 470 million crowns in the first seven months of 1997, according to the company's general manager, Jaroslav Petros. The damages caused by thje flooding amount to 78 million crowns, he added.

- Lockheed Martin, one of the serious contenders for the multi-million dollar contract for the sale of fighter aircraft to the Czech army, will be opening a permanent office in Prague in the middle of September, according to the Czech representative of Lockheed, Jan Ploc.
